thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx and tail latency affecting eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. Error rate spike starting at 1832509700, impacting model-serving paths. Paging oncall SRE.
alice.sre: saw the alert. Looking at dashboards now. KPIs: p95 latency up from 220ms -> 850ms for text-gen, 5xx rate ~7% in eu-west over last 5m.
bob.sre: I also see a Provider A upstream error increase for long-seq requests. Provider B healthy but capacity limited for high-memory models.
carol.infra: network telemetry shows increased packet retries from eu-west -> provider-a-eu cluster. Possibly transient network degradation at provider.
alice.sre: initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle long-context requests in eu-west for non-enterprise plans 2) start partial drain of provider-a in eu-west (move new connections to provider-b) 3) enable fallback short-context model variant for heavy requests 4) notify support + customers.
support-ops: can we confirm customer impact? Are API keys returning 429 or 5xx? Need list of affected customers.
bob.sre: mix of 429s (rate limits) and 502/504 from upstream. 5xx mostly from provider-a. 429s are mostly from our automatic quota enforcement when requests retried; we'll throttle to avoid overload.
alice.sre: taking step 1 now: applying dynamic rate-limit policy for eu-west for non-paid tiers. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.internal/rate-limits/apply -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","policy":"throttle-long-ctx","max_tps":12}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SERV_OPS_TOKEN'
```
deploy-bot: rate-limit-policy applied to eu-west-1 (id: rlp-2026-03-13-01). Rolling update on 4 edge-routers.
carol.infra: starting provider drain for provider-a in eu-west. Using graceful drain with 60s connection window. Command: 
```
./providerctl drain --provider provider-a --region eu-west-1 --grace 60s --target provider-b
```
deploy-bot: drain initiated for provider-a eu-west-1. New connections will be routed to provider-b. Existing requests allowed to finish for 60s.
dave.prod: heads-up: we should disable heavy embeddings-batch endpoint (embed.v2/batch) in eu-west for next 15m. High cost, low priority during incident.
alice.sre: disabling embeddings batch in eu-west for non-enterprise. Patch: `feature-flag embeddings-batch eu-west off --scope non-enterprise`.
deploy-bot: feature flag updated: embeddings-batch disabled for non-enterprise in eu-west.
bob.sre: I'm also enabling adaptive traffic shaping at the edge to favor short-seq chat flows. Config snippet: 
```
edge.shaper.set(region="eu-west-1",weights={"chat":0.7,"text-gen":0.3})
```
carol.infra: provider-a connection error rate falling after drain started. Upstream 5xx from provider-a decreased from 6.8% -> 2.1% in next 90s.
support-ops: notified top 10 customers impacted in EU (apps with >1000 rps). Sending template message to enterprise contacts with mitigation steps and ETA for resolution. :email: 
support-ops: message sent to affected customers: "We’re experiencing higher latency/5xx in EU; we are routing traffic to an alternate provider and throttling heavy requests temporarily. No action required; you may see increased latency or 429s for very large requests."
alice.sre: on-call handoff: I'm going to stay on for stabilization but handing primary to bob.sre for monitoring and follow-up. bob, please take over post-incident chat and coordinate any scaling with infra.
bob.sre: taking over. Watching metrics. Will escalate to infra if p95 > 1s for next 5m.
carol.infra: we've increased provider-b pool in eu-west by +3 nodes (hot-spare). Scaling command: `infractl scale provider-b eu-west +3`. Estimated warmup ~45s.
deploy-bot: scale request accepted, nodes provisioning. New instances joining service.
bob.sre: p95 dropped to ~420ms after shaping and drainage. 5xx down to 0.9% across region. Good trend but not fully back to baseline.
alice.sre: next steps: keep throttle and embedding ban for 10 more minutes, let drain complete, then gradually relax if stable. Create incident ticket and assign postmortem to alice.sre + carol.infra.
support-ops: customers want ETA. Suggest telling them we'll re-evaluate in 20m and provide a follow-up.
bob.sre: agreed. Setting monitoring alerts to tighter windows and enabling verbose logs for flows hitting fallback models.
alice.sre: starting to re-enable embeddings-batch for enterprise only to avoid breaking paid SLAs: `feature-flag embeddings-batch eu-west on --scope enterprise`.
deploy-bot: feature flag change applied.
carol.infra: provider-b capacity holding, traffic normalized to ~85% of baseline. No further errors from provider-a once drain finished. Provider-a still reporting degraded NIC but isolated.
dave.prod: product note: some low-priority customers might see truncated responses if they hit short-context fallback; mention in postmortem.
alice.sre: resolution: mitigation successful, traffic routed away from degraded provider, throttles and feature toggles will be relaxed after 20m of stable metrics. Creating follow-up ticket for root-cause with infra/provider contact details.
bob.sre: closing the live coordination channel. Will post final status update and move to #postmortems once root-cause analysis starts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied, region eu-west-1 traffic partially failed over to provider-b; 5xx rate reduced to <1%. Monitoring for 20m. Incident severity lowered to P1->P2.
alice.sre: filing postmortem draft, will include timelines, customer impact summary, and action items: 1) provider network follow-up 2) improve auto-failover thresholds 3) add synthetic tests for long-seq traffic. :memo: 
support-ops: follow-up sent to affected customers with updated ETA and link to incident page.
bob.sre: handoff complete. Leaving the channel open for any late regressions until 1832510480.
